title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: A ton of rubber black is priced like an industrial input; a ton of conductive or specialty black is priced like a performance guarantee.
epigraph.author: Specialty Materials Industry Axiom

web_blocks.html: PCBL Chemical runs three active revenue engines plus an early-stage battery materials arm. The three active engines are: (1) Carbon Black (tire, rubber, and specialty grades), (2) Captive Green Power Co-generation, and (3) Specialty Water, Detergent & Oilfield Chemicals in Aquapharm Chemical Limited. Alongside them, PCBL is building a fourth option in battery materials via Nanovace Technologies and Acetylene Black. In FY26, consolidated revenue stood at ₹8,189 crore (recovering to ₹8,860 crore TTM through September 2026). Carbon black volumes hit a record 618,956 MT, while Aquapharm added ₹1,443 crore (~17.6% of consolidated revenue).

web_blocks.html: Rubber-grade carbon black is the volume core, making up ~88.7% of PCBL's 618,956 MT sales in FY26. Made by burning heavy aromatic oils (CBFS) in high-heat reactors, rubber black makes up 25%–30% of a modern tire by weight. It gives tires tensile strength, wear resistance, and heat control. A radial truck tire cannot run at highway speeds without grade-specific carbon black. PCBL sells to Indian tire majors and global OEMs, splitting FY26–H1 FY27 volume roughly two-thirds domestic and one-third export. In Q1 FY27, total carbon black volume reached 153,530 MT [7, 8]. In Q2 FY27, PCBL cut low-margin spot exports 18% QoQ to 41,337 MT against 92,843 MT domestic (134,180 MT total) [6, 7].

Specialty carbon black is PCBL's main organic margin driver. With capacity expanded to 112,000 MTPA (including 20,000 MTPA added at Mundra), PCBL sold 69,635 MT of specialty grades in FY26 (~11.3% of carbon black volume, with Q4 FY26 reaching 19,000 MT, up 26% YoY). Unlike tire blacks, specialty grades ship in smaller lots for non-rubber uses. They add jetness and UV protection to black HDPE pipes, tint car paints and inks, and give controlled conductivity in high-voltage power cables. Winning approval for a single specialty grade takes 12 to 24 months, creating much higher switching costs than standard ASTM rubber grades.

Aquapharm Chemical Limited marks PCBL's move outside carbon chemistry. It runs plants in India (Pune/Mahad/Pirangut), the US (Texas), and Saudi Arabia (Jeddah) with ~130,000 MTPA base capacity plus 38,000 MTPA of brownfield additions. Aquapharm makes three product lines. First, organophosphonates (HEDP, ATMP, DETPMP under Aquacid) stop scale buildup in boilers, cooling towers, and desalination membranes. Second, green chelates (GLDA, HEIDA, IDS) replace banned phosphates and EDTA in dishwasher pods and laundry liquids for P&G, Unilever, and Henkel. Third, oilfield chemicals (imidazolines, quats, scale inhibitors) protect oil and gas wells from mineral scaling. Roughly 50% of Aquapharm's sales come from North America, 20% from Europe, 17% from India, and 13% from the rest of the world.

Finally, PCBL is building a battery and conductive materials arm for EVs and grid storage. Beyond Energia conductive grades and a planned 1,000 MTPA super-conductive line, PCBL signed a tech deal with China's Ningxia Jinhua Chemical for a 5,000 MTPA Acetylene Black plant. Acetylene Black is an ultra-pure additive used in LFP/NMC lithium-ion cathodes and high-voltage cables. At the same time, majority-owned Nanovace Technologies Ltd. (with a Palej pilot plant and US patents) is developing nano-silicon anode materials with 5–6x the energy density of graphite. While aligned with India's EV cell push, these battery units are pre-commercial and remain long-term options rather than near-term profit drivers.

web_blocks.title: Why Segment Mix Matters More Than Headline Revenue
paragraphs: Because carbon black prices pass through crude and CBFS moves, headline sales can swing without showing true volume health. For example, FY26 sales dipped 3% to ₹8,189 crore even though carbon black volumes hit a record 618,956 MT.
On the other hand, Aquapharm gets 50% of its sales from North America and 20% from Europe. That exposes PCBL to US rig counts and European factory slowdowns that have no link to Indian tire demand.

book_paragraphs: If someone asks you what PCBL Chemical actually makes, the cleanest answer is that it sells engineered molecules that stop things from wearing out, scaling up, or short-circuiting. About 82% of its ₹8,189 crore FY26 revenue still comes from carbon black and the captive power generated alongside it, while the remaining ~18% comes from Aquapharm's water-treatment, detergent, and oilfield chemicals. Yet lumping those together hides four very different economic engines under one roof.

The foundation is rubber-grade carbon black—roughly 549,000 tonnes of PCBL's record 618,956 tonnes sold in FY26. Picture a highway truck tire: nearly a third of its weight is carbon black, mixed into natural and synthetic rubber so the tread resists tearing, conducts heat away from the road, and survives tens of thousands of kilometers. PCBL supplies Indian and global tire makers from five strategically located plants—Durgapur in the east, Kochi in the south, Palej and Mundra in Gujarat, and its automated brownfield facility in Tamil Nadu. Because tire companies buy on formula-linked contracts that pass through raw material costs, rubber black is a volume-and-utilization business. Keep the reactors running at 97% to 99%, capture the waste tail gas to run 122 MW of captive green power plants, and you earn a reliable baseline spread.

On top of that commodity base sits specialty carbon black—69,635 tonnes in FY26, backed by 112,000 tonnes of dedicated capacity. Here, the customer is not a tire factory; it is an HDPE pipe extruder who needs UV protection so buried telecom conduits do not crack, an automotive paint formulator chasing deep-black gloss, or a high-voltage cable maker needing semi-conductive shielding. Qualifying a single specialty grade can take a customer one to two years of lab and line trials. Once you are designed into the formulation, you are rarely swapped out for a 2% price cut, which is why specialty grades earn more than double the EBITDA per tonne of standard rubber black.

The third pillar is Aquapharm, which contributed ₹1,443 crore of revenue in FY26. Aquapharm does not touch carbon reactors at all; it works with phosphorus and amino-acid chemistry across plants in Maharashtra, Texas, and Saudi Arabia. Its phosphonates keep mineral scale from choking industrial cooling towers and reverse-osmosis desalination plants. Its biodegradable green chelates—molecules like GLDA and IDS—go into eco-friendly dishwasher tablets and liquid detergents for Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and Henkel. And its oilfield chemicals keep US shale wells and pipelines free of carbonate scale. Because roughly 50% of Aquapharm's sales are in North America and 20% in Europe, its earnings dance to US drilling rig counts and Western consumer-chemical restocking rather than Indian auto sales.

Finally, management is laying down a fourth, longer-dated bet in battery materials. Through a technology transfer with China's Ningxia Jinhua Chemical, PCBL is building a 5,000-tonne Acetylene Black line for lithium-ion battery conductivity, alongside a pilot plant at Palej under Nanovace Technologies to make nano-silicon anode materials. Silicon can theoretically hold five to six times more lithium than graphite, making it one of the most sought-after chemistries for next-generation EV cells. Still, you and I should keep our feet on the ground: battery qualification cycles are brutal and slow, so Nanovace is an intriguing call option on 2028–2030, not a cash cow for today.

Walk through a radial tire plant in Chennai or Pune with me to see why PCBL's standard carbon black is never an afterthought. Every passenger-car radial tire requires roughly 25% to 30% carbon black by weight—blended with natural and synthetic rubber to prevent tread abrasion, dissipate heat at highway speeds, and protect sidewalls from ultraviolet cracking.

If a single batch of N220 or N330 carbon black varies in particle size or structure, a tire maker risks warranty recalls and blowout liability. That is why OEM qualification takes twelve to twenty-four months of lab, drum, and road testing, creating sticky multi-year relationships that reward scale and consistency.

Now contrast that with Aquapharm's phosphonates and oilfield polymers. In the Permian Basin or a European municipal water plant, Aquapharm competes against global specialty chemical incumbents on formulation speed, regulatory registration, and customer-site service—a very different commercial muscle where PCBL is still proving its ability to restore the 20% EBITDA margins Aquapharm enjoyed before the buyout.

book_subsections.title: Why Tire Makers Cannot Replace Carbon Black — and Why Battery Cells Might Need More of It
paragraphs: Every few years, someone asks whether electric vehicles or silica-reinforced green tires will make carbon black obsolete. Let us separate physics from headlines. In passenger car tires, precipitated silica has indeed replaced part of the carbon black in low-rolling-resistance tread compounds, especially in Europe. Yet in truck and bus radials, off-the-road mining tires, and tire sidewalls—the heaviest part of the global tire market—carbon black remains irreplaceable because silica cannot match its UV protection, thermal conductivity, and tear resistance. Moreover, electric vehicles are heavier than internal-combustion cars and deliver instant torque, which wears tires down 15%–20% faster, shortening replacement cycles.

At the same time, EV batteries create a brand-new, high-purity demand vector. Inside every lithium-ion cell, active cathode and anode particles are poor electrical conductors on their own; they require a conductive carbon network—using super-conductive furnace black, acetylene black, or carbon nanotubes—to move electrons efficiently during fast charging. By securing Ningxia Jinhua's acetylene black technology and investing in Nanovace's nano-silicon anode precursors, PCBL is trying to follow the electron from the tire tread into the battery pack. Just keep in mind that qualifying a conductive additive with a Tier-1 battery gigafactory takes years of safety and cycle-life testing, so revenue contribution will be back-ended.

book_subsections.title: Inside the Specialty Carbon Black & Conductive Additives Frontier
paragraphs: To understand why equity analysts get excited about PCBL's specialty grades even when consolidated profits look sluggish, you and I have to step away from the tire factory and look at wire-and-cable jacketing, engineering plastics, and lithium-ion battery cathodes. Unlike commodity rubber black, which sells in twenty-tonne bulk bags on formula contracts, specialty black is sold in smaller lots with tailored surface area, jetness, and electrical conductivity.

Take an automotive high-voltage EV cable sheath or a food-contact HDPE pipe. The compounder needs carbon black with ultra-low polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and tight grit specifications so the extruded polymer does not develop pinholes under dielectric stress. Switching suppliers mid-program risks failing UL or automotive OEM certification, which explains why specialty grades earn two to three times the EBITDA per tonne of standard tread grades.

The next frontier is Nanovace Technologies—PCBL's joint venture targeting acetylene black and nano-silicon/conductive carbon additives for lithium-ion batteries. With US patents secured and a pilot plant running at Palej, Nanovace represents genuine long-term option value. Still, you and I must keep our analytical feet on the ground: pilot plants do not pay down ₹5,083 Cr of debt today, and commercial-scale battery qualification with global cell makers typically takes three to five years.

book_callouts.title: Four Chemistries, One Balance Sheet
book_callouts.text: PCBL is no longer a single-product tire ancillary. You are underwriting four distinct businesses sharing one balance sheet:
bullets: Rubber Carbon Black (~89% of CB volume): high utilization, pass-through pricing, cyclical export spreads.
Specialty Carbon Black (~11% of CB volume): sticky OEM qualifications, >2x unit margins.
Aquapharm (~18% of consolidated sales): US/EU-exposed phosphonates, green chelates, and oilfield chemicals.
Battery Materials (Acetylene Black & Nanovace): early-stage EV optionality requiring patient capex.
